working_title: Suffolk's Golf Coast: A Practical Guide to Playing Felixstowe, Aldeburgh, Thorpeness and Royal Worlington
angle: Suffolk is quietly one of England's most varied golf counties, with a true links, a heathland-links hybrid in the UK top 100, a world-renowned nine-holer, and a James Braid resort course all within easy driving distance of each other. The post makes the case for a dedicated Suffolk golf trip and tells visitors exactly what they need to know before they book.
research_notes:
- Suffolk has around 33 affiliated golf clubs ranging from 9-hole layouts to championship courses (stayinsuffolk.com, 2026)
- Felixstowe Ferry Golf Club (est. 1880): the only true links course in Suffolk and the 5th oldest club in England; 18-hole Martello Championship course (par 72, designed by Henry Cotton, 6,379 yds) plus the 9-hole Kingsfleet pay-and-play course; visitors welcome on both, advance contact advised; set in an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty with views over the River Deben; awarded Championship Venue of the Year by England Golf in 2018
- Aldeburgh Golf Club (est. 1884): described as England's second-oldest maritime heathland course; championship course is a heathland-links hybrid, par 68 (men's card), no par 5s, characterised by dense gorse-lined fairways; ranked in the UK top 100; visitors welcome with handicap certificate, weekdays and weekends; also has the 9-hole River Course (no bunkers, overlooks the River Alde, suitable for higher handicappers)
- Thorpeness Hotel & Golf Club: James Braid design (1922), par 70, approx. 6,474 yards; one of the finest and most challenging courses in East Anglia; open to the public; notable landmark is the 'House in the Clouds' visible on the finishing hole; the course was voted 'greenest golf club in Britain' in the 2012 STRI Golf Environment Awards
- Royal Worlington & Newmarket Golf Club ('The Sacred Nine'): 9-hole private inland links near Bury St Edmunds, est. 1893; designed by Tom Dunn with refinements by H.S. Colt; consistently ranked in the UK top 100; described by Bernard Darwin as 'The Sacred Nine'; home club of the Cambridge University golf team; Royal prefix granted by Queen Victoria in 1895; visitors must arrange visits in advance with the Secretary; three- and four-ball play is not permitted (foursomes and twosomes only); 18 holes for visitors means two loops of the 9; visitor green fees (2025 data): weekdays £120, weekends £140 for the equivalent of 18 holes
- Aldeburgh and Thorpeness are approximately 1.5 miles apart on the Suffolk coast, making them a natural two-day pairing
- Felixstowe is approx. 12 miles east of Ipswich off the A14; Royal Worlington is inland near Mildenhall, approx. 40 miles from the coast — so a logical circuit covers both coast and inland in a 2–3 night trip
- Suffolk coast enjoys some of the driest weather in the British Isles
- Visitors to Aldeburgh's championship course should note that fourball play is restricted to certain days only — a practical point worth flagging
- Royal Worlington: visits must be arranged in advance with the Secretary; smart-casual dress code enforced; pace of play expected (18 holes typically completed in 3 hours)
- Style variety across the four clubs: true links (Felixstowe), heathland-links hybrid (Aldeburgh), heathland resort (Thorpeness), inland links (Royal Worlington) — a genuinely diverse county for a golf trip
must_avoid:
- Do not fabricate current green fees for Aldeburgh or Thorpeness; only Royal Worlington (£120/£140, 2025 data flagged) and a Felixstowe guide price from Golfshake are available — describe others in general terms.
- No invented quotes from members, pros, or reviewers.
- No gambling/betting content.
- No medical or injury advice beyond generic warm-up guidance.
- No financial advice on affordability of the trip.
- No affiliate links unless the operator or product is in /src/content/approved-partners.md; any informational mentions of courses should carry no affiliate link and no editorial comment drawing attention to the absence of one.
- Do not imply the site owner has personally played any of these courses.
- Royal Worlington is a private club — post must make clear that advance booking via the Secretary is required, and that three- and four-balls are not permitted, to avoid frustrating readers who show up unannounced.
